processing: Gongfu black tea from the Qianmei clonal cultivars, its method combining Meitan's older Mei Hong approach with those of Zhenghe, Tanyang and Keemun gongfu teas.
harvest_season: Little is documented for picking dates; as with most premium Guizhou gongfu black teas, spring lots are prized.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight dark strips, typical of a premium gongfu tea, often with golden tips.
appearance_liquor: Clear amber to orange, as is typical of a gongfu black tea.
taste_profile: Mellow gongfu black tea, its makers aiming for Keemun-like aroma with the finesse of Zhenghe gongfu; expect a sweet, clean cup.

brewing.notes: Gaiwan, short steeps; it also brews well Western-style for about three minutes.

vintage_note: Sold as a recent harvest, usually with spring lots at the top and with grades set by the maker. It is a protected name, and also a commercial one, so check for the mark and the maker. It is not an ageing tea, and is best within about two years.
description:
Zunyi Hong is a modern gongfu black tea from northern Guizhou, centred on Meitan County but protected across several Zunyi counties. The name plays on Zunyi's 'red' revolutionary associations as well as on red tea, the Chinese term for black tea.

It is made from the local Qianmei clonal cultivars. The makers set out to combine Meitan's older black tea methods with those of Zhenghe, Tanyang and Keemun, which makes it a deliberately designed tea rather than a village tradition.

In the cup, look for clean sweetness and a soft aroma. Water just below the boil and short steeps are safest, and a good lot should stay pleasant through several rounds.

The protected area includes Meitan, Fenggang, Yuqing, Daozhen, Zheng'an, Wuchuan and Xishui. Maker and grade are what separate a good one from an ordinary one, so compare before paying a premium.
history:
The tea has been developed since 2008, drawing on Meitan's 1940s black tea work. Meitan Shengxing Tea is named as the developer, and the tea took a special jury prize in the 2009 'top ten Guizhou teas' selection.

When the 2015 Milan Expo held a centenary tea award, the Zunyi Hong public brand was among the gold medal winners, alongside Meitan Cui Ya. Claims of a much longer company lineage come from promotional writing and do not match this record.
